new_statements.rule_in_words: The only published statement is a dialect-survey remark: in Kumalu (and its Mumengtein and Pelenkwa sub-varieties) some words stress the initial syllable, unlike Patep, where the initial syllable is an unstressed schwa and stress falls on a later full-vowel syllable. No rule is given. The authors' own Kumalu transcriptions (pp. 18-19) mark stress on the first syllable in some disyllables ('iob 'sun', 'laga? 'cloud', 'tika 'one', 'mendeŋ 'four', 'balu 'five', 'nemalu 'ten') and on the last in others (ne'ma 'hand', ba'ga 'foot', ndε'ndu? 'moon', la'li 'meat', lε'nzi 'fat'), so stress is not fixed to one edge and is not predictable from vowel quality alone (ne'ma has two full vowels). Provisional: variable stress, position undetermined.
new_statements.exceptions: Only 'for some words'; the survey does not say which class of words or why. Chart F (p. 12) also lists Kumalu word-final unstressed vowel + nasal (Vn) where Patep has V#.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level, elicited citation forms in a comparative wordlist (survey, not a phonological description). The source is a dialect survey of the Mumeng chain, first-hand by the authors (SIL, Patep team), not a phonology of Kumalu.
new_statements.identity_note: The statement covers Kumalu together with its sub-varieties Mumengtein and Pelenkwa (Adams & Lauck treat Pelenkwa and Mumengtein as one subdialect of Kumalu, p. 10; McElhanon 1984 lists them under 'Mumeng (Kumalu)'), all within kuma1278. It is a contrast against Patep (ISO ptp; Glottolog places Patep under the Mumeng group mume1239, sister to Dambi-Kumaru damb1252), whose phonemic statement (Lauck & Adams 1975) is the only full phonology in the chain and does not describe Kumalu.

readall_conflicts: The only direct Kumalu evidence remains Adams & Lauck 1985 (existing statement): it says Kumalu, Mumengtein and Pelenkwa have a stress pattern different from Patep's, and its Kumalu wordlist marks initial stress on some items ('iob 'sun', 'tika 'one', 'balu 'five') and final stress on others (ne'ma 'hand', ba'ga 'foot', la'li 'meat'). taken together with the 1985 remark, that Patep rule is precisely what Kumalu is said to differ from, so it must not be recorded as the Kumalu rule. Hooley & McElhanon 1970 is silent; the SIL-PNG page could not be opened. No source opened gives a Kumalu-specific placement rule.
